title: Ring pooling: the place description keeps WHERE in the frame things are (centre / middle ring / edge), not one average over the whole 128 m frame
hypothesis: Experiments 12-16 took held-out truedop_2024 from 10.75% to 86.75% usable (exp 16: mission 0.155, usable 0.8675, false fix 0.0225, abstain 0.11) by improving only the trunk, and the three training photographs now sit at 100% usable / 0% false fix on the same held-out viewpoints, so what is left is purely the survey gap. One stage has never been questioned in the whole era: every member's place feature is a GLOBAL AVERAGE (GAP) of its 14x14 and 7x7 trunk maps. GAP is an orderless bag of local features: it says WHICH roofs, trees, road surfaces and shadows are in the 128 m frame, but not where. That is exactly the part of the description that a new survey corrupts (season changes canopy, sun angle changes shadows, cars and construction differ), while the part a new survey preserves - the spatial arrangement of buildings, streets and blocks relative to the point the aircraft is over - is thrown away. GAP was the natural choice because frames arrive at arbitrary headings and an average is rotation-invariant; but rotation invariance does not need orderlessness. Concentric-ring pooling (mean over the centre disc, the middle annulus and the outer ring, separately, then concatenated) is equally invariant to heading about the frame centre and keeps the radial layout: 'a courtyard under me, a block of flat roofs around it, a wide road at the edge' instead of 'some courtyard, some roofs, some road'. The frame centre is by construction the labelled position (training views are rotated about the crop centre, eval error is measured at the crop centre), so the centre ring in particular carries the most position-specific content, and neighbouring cells that share the same bag of textures but differ in arrangement become separable. I expect this to (a) convert part of the 11% abstentions, which on this design are frames where the two members or the 3x3 block split their belief between look-alike places, into confident correct fixes, and (b) not raise false fixes, since the confidence gate is unchanged. Builds on the experiment 12-16 lineage (trunk, committee, cosine head and MixStyle all kept as-is); no earlier-era experiment changed the pooling of a pretrained trunk, so this is new on any ruler.
method: In model/model.py Member.embed only: replace the two GAP reductions (.mean(dim=(2,3))) with fixed, parameter-free, rotation-invariant concentric-ring pooling. For each read level (mid 14x14 after features[13], deep 7x7 after features[17], both at the 224 px input), three fixed ring masks over the grid are registered as buffers: cell centre (i+0.5, j+0.5), frame centre (H/2, W/2), radius r normalised by the inscribed half-width H/2; ring 0 = r < 1/3, ring 1 = 1/3 <= r < 2/3, ring 2 = r >= 2/3 (includes the corners). Each mask is normalised to sum 1, so ring k's output is the mean of the lifted feature over that ring. The lifted 56-channel map of each level becomes 56 x 3 = 168 numbers; the place feature f is the concatenation of both levels, 336-d (was 112). EMBED_DIM becomes 336; the BatchNorm1d, cosine-prototype matrix (n_cells x 336) and offset head grow accordingly. Nothing else changes: trunk, lifts, MixStyle, 128->224 resize, committee, cosine scale/margin, block decode, confidence gate, losses, augmentation, epochs.
expected_outcome: mission_score 0.155 -> ~0.10-0.12 on truedop_2024: usable_fix_rate 0.8675 -> ~0.90 (abstentions 11% -> ~8%), false_fix_rate stays <= 0.025, median error roughly flat or slightly lower (~30-34 m; the cell head, not the pooling, sets the resolution). train_capture_diagnostics stay at ~0.000 (100% usable). Training-time top1 should rise faster per epoch than exp 16 (0.894 at epoch 8). Refutation: if usable on 2024 does not rise (or falls) while training-capture top1 rises, the radial layout is itself survey-specific at this resolution (e.g. shadows displace edges) and the orderless average was the more survey-robust summary - which would be informative: it points at the trunk/training signal, not the pooling, as the remaining lever. Model size ~17.4 MB -> ~23 MB fp32 (prototypes 2970x336 per member), well under the 32 MiB gate; host latency essentially unchanged (~22 ms).
init_strategy: pretrained:mobilenet_v2 IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..17] (torchvision, BSD-3), unchanged from experiment 16
eli5: Until now each navigator described a photo by tipping all its little observations into one bag - 'there are flat roofs, some trees, a wide road' - without saying where in the picture they were. A new survey changes many of those observations (leaves, shadows, parked cars) but not the layout of the city. Now the navigator keeps three bags instead of one: what is right underneath, what is in a ring around that, and what is at the edge. That still works whichever way the drone is facing, but it describes the arrangement of the place, which stays the same from one photograph to the next.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: NEW: how the description is summarised. As before, the 128 px frame is enlarged to 224 px and read by two independent copies of MobileNetV2 (pre-trained on ImageNet, open BSD-3 licence, fine-tuned on Berlin at a tenth of the usual learning rate), at two depths: a 96-channel 14×14 map and a 320-channel 7×7 map, each lifted to 56 numbers per spot. Instead of averaging each map over the whole frame, it is now averaged separately over three concentric rings - the centre (what is right under the drone), a middle ring, and the outer edge - which still does not depend on which way the drone faces but keeps the layout. 56 numbers × 3 rings × 2 depths = a 336-number description of the place (was 112)

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: each extractor's description is centred, scaled to unit length and compared by angle against one unit-length reference direction per map tile (~3,000 tiles, 128 m each) - a compass, not a lookup table; the angle match times a fixed sharpness (30) is the tile score. The two members' tile-belief maps are averaged to pick the tile. (Reference directions are now 336 numbers long to match the description)

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the averaged belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head per member that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot; the two nudges are averaged

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the SMALLER of the two members' belief on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — both navigators must independently back the same place; if either one spreads its belief elsewhere the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: unchanged from experiment 16: cross-survey style mixing inside the feature extractor after MobileNetV2's 3rd, 6th and 10th blocks (training only), angular-margin tile loss, offset loss, paired three-survey batches, re-photographing augmentation, pre-trained blocks at a tenth of the learning rate; targets, epochs and views per epoch unchanged. Training views are enlarged to 224 px exactly as in flight

implementation_brief:
ONE change: replace global average pooling in Member.embed with fixed concentric-ring pooling. Files: model/model.py (main change), model/train.py (only constants/log strings/metadata that assume a 112-d feature or GAP).

model/model.py:
1. Constants: add N_RINGS = 3 and RING_EDGES = (1/3, 2/3) (normalised radius thresholds). Change LIFT_DIM to a literal 56 (it is currently EMBED_DIM // 2; decouple it), and set EMBED_DIM = 2 * LIFT_DIM * N_RINGS (= 336). Keep MID_HW/DEEP_HW logic consistent: the mid map is INPUT_PX//16 = 14, the deep map INPUT_PX//32 = 7 (add MID_HW = INPUT_PX // 16 and DEEP_HW = INPUT_PX // 32 to model.py if convenient; train.py already defines its own copies, which may stay or import these).
2. Add a module-level helper `ring_masks(hw: int) -> torch.Tensor` returning float32 [N_RINGS, hw*hw]: for grid cell (i, j) with centre (i+0.5, j+0.5), frame centre c = hw/2, r = sqrt((i+0.5-c)^2 + (j+0.5-c)^2) / (hw/2); ring 0 = r < 1/3, ring 1 = 1/3 <= r < 2/3, ring 2 = r >= 2/3 (corners included). Each row normalised to sum to 1. Assert every ring has >= 1 cell (expected counts: 14x14 -> 16/44/136-ish; 7x7 -> 5/16/28; exact numbers are whatever the formula gives — just assert non-empty). Flatten order must match tensor.flatten(2) of an [B,C,H,W] map (row-major over H then W).
3. In Member.__init__: register two non-persistent-or-persistent buffers (either is fine, they must bake into the ONNX as constants): self.register_buffer('ring_mid', ring_masks(MID_HW)) and self.register_buffer('ring_deep', ring_masks(DEEP_HW)). self.embed_bn = nn.BatchNorm1d(EMBED_DIM), self.prototypes [n_cells, EMBED_DIM], self.off_head = nn.Linear(EMBED_DIM, 2) — these already use EMBED_DIM, so they grow automatically; verify.
4. Add a method `_ring_pool(self, h, masks)`: h [B, C, H, W] -> h.flatten(2) [B, C, H*W] @ masks.t() [H*W, K] -> [B, C, K] -> .flatten(1) [B, C*K]. Use torch.matmul (exports as a plain ONNX MatMul). Assert at trace time that H*W == masks.shape[1] so a wrong INPUT_PX fails loudly.
5. In Member.embed, replace
   f = torch.cat([self.lift_mid(h_mid).mean(dim=(2, 3)), self.lift_deep(h_deep).mean(dim=(2, 3))], dim=1)
   with
   f = torch.cat([self._ring_pool(self.lift_mid(h_mid), self.ring_mid), self._ring_pool(self.lift_deep(h_deep), self.ring_deep)], dim=1)  # [B, 336]
   Everything else in embed (resize to INPUT_PX, ImageNet normalisation, block-by-block loop with MixStyle after features[3]/[6]/[10], h_mid after features[13]) stays exactly as is. e = F.normalize(self.embed_bn(f), dim=1) unchanged.
6. Update the module docstring: add a 'RING POOLING (capture-holdout era, experiment 17)' paragraph describing the change (three fixed concentric rings per read level, rotation-invariant about the frame centre, normalised masks, 56 x 3 x 2 = 336-d place feature, parameter-free) and fix the Member docstring's 'GAP' wording. Do not touch anything else: trunk construction/loading (mnv2_features17.pt, strict), MixStyle, CellLocNet (committee, block_mask, forward decode, confidence = min member block mass), loss_fn, COS_SCALE/COS_MARGIN, export_onnx, estimate_position.

model/train.py:
- Do NOT change the training loop, augmentation, optimiser groups (lifts/embed_bn/prototypes/off_head are head params, ring buffers are not parameters), LR schedule, epochs, batch size, targets, or survey_diag logic. Ring masks are buffers, so they move with model.to(device) automatically.
- Update only what references the old 112-d / GAP design: the startup print line (say 'ring-pooled x3' and the 336-d feature), and the train_info metadata strings ('trunk', 'capture_sampling') to mention concentric-ring pooling (3 rings) -> 336-d place feature; add 'n_rings': 3 and 'ring_edges': [1/3, 2/3] to train_info. If survey_diag or any diagnostic hard-codes 112 or calls .mean(dim=(2,3)) on trunk maps to rebuild the feature, route it through member.embed() instead so it uses the ring pooling.

FIXED CONTRACTS (restate, must hold):
- train.py CLI unchanged: python -m model.train --area berlin --out-dir runs/<id> [--epochs N] (and the existing other flags); it writes <out>/models/berlin.onnx and the train_info JSON as today.
- ONNX export contract (model.py docstring): input 'frame' 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1]; output 'uvc' [[u, v, conf]] with u, v normalised map coords in [0,1] and conf in [0,1]; the whole decode stays inside the graph; opset 17, dynamo=False. The 128->224 resize stays in-graph.
- Training reads ONLY buckets(meta, 'train'). Nothing under model/ may open the eval capture truedop_2024 in any form.
- Deployment gates: exported fp32 ONNX <= 32 MiB (expect ~23 MB: +2 x 2970 x 224 extra prototype floats), host latency <= 250 ms (expect ~22 ms, unchanged).
- Sanity check before handing back (CPU, tiny): build the model from the Berlin meta, run a 2x3x128x128 random batch through forward() in eval mode -> shape [2, 3], conf in [0,1]; confirm each member's embed returns f of shape [B, 336]; and confirm rotation invariance of the pooling itself: for a random [1, C, 14, 14] tensor, ring-pooling it and its torch.rot90 give identical outputs (the masks are symmetric under 90-degree rotation by construction — assert it).
